findings.reason: a mechanism with no asserted caller is the plan's own third reasoning check failing at the gate, so the section needs a case (or a named assertion) that the shell's poll invokes the refresh and replaces `window.STATE.schedule`.
findings.text: the deliverable's mechanism is "the shell calls [the refresh functions] on its poll", but every §11 case for it is "a loader case" under `node`, which runs `docs/ui/state-loader.js` alone and cannot execute `docs/ui/shell.jsx`; nothing in the section asserts the shell calls the new functions, so a node can land the loader functions with no production caller, pass the whole §11 gate, and still leave the schedule stale between document changes on a quiet view — exactly the failure the section exists to prevent

findings.reason: the section's threshold can be met by a build that multiplies the schedule traffic it was written to cut, so the acceptance must count `/_schedule` requests (or the done-when must assert the route is fetched only while the crew view is open).
findings.text: the only acceptance number is "the coordinator counts `/_index/power_convertor` requests … less those page loads", which measures the removal of the fleet-driven refetch and nothing about the churn the new route adds; the deliverable bounds that churn ("at least once a minute while the crew view is open", not on every 3 s poll and not off the crew route), yet the shell's poll at `docs/ui/shell.jsx:298` is mounted at the shell root and runs on every route, so a node that fetches `/_schedule` unconditionally from that poll passes every §11 case and the acceptance clause while issuing ~600 requests in the 30 minutes counted

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_attach_schedule_for_read` resolves at `reckon/serve.py:1777` and is called with `reference=datetime.now(UTC)` at the discovery read (`reckon/serve.py:3332`), the shell's 3 s `/crew` poll resolves at `docs/ui/shell.jsx:298`, `docs/ui/crew.jsx:44` does read `window.STATE.schedule`, `BOUND = 50_000` resolves in `tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` (measured serve.py 45,882 estimated tokens, ~4,100 under the bound), and `tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py` / `tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py` exist with harnesses that can host the cases named.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11's new loader cases drive state-loader.js functions directly, so nothing in the section shows the shell's `/crew` poll ever calls them, and the section's only acceptance count reads `/_index`, which the new `/_schedule` route never touches, so the churn the route introduces is unmeasured.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log sits under the run directory and ends in `EXIT=`, and the acceptance count is read from the served request log rather than a scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `/_schedule/<project>`, the stale rule and the loader's refresh functions name the mechanism, and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag enters a symbol, filename or comment §11 will write.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. The root cause matches the cited code (`docs/ui/state-loader.js:747-759` dispatches `reckon-fleet` and then calls the same `refetchDerived()` a `change` event calls, and `_attach_schedule_for_read` → `_crew_rows` rebuilds the schedule per read), each bullet's mechanism can produce its measure (the `/crew` rows carry `project`, `plan` and `phase`, so the crew view can see a run-set or phase change and drive an `/_index`-free `/_schedule` fetch), and the caller is real and named — the shell's single `/crew` poll at `docs/ui/shell.jsx:298-315`; the schedule has no consumer outside `docs/ui/crew.jsx` (grep for `.schedule` across `docs/ui/*.jsx` returns only crew.jsx and state-loader.js), so decoupling it from fleet events is safe.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11's three bullets are one behaviour (a project-scoped schedule route, its two consumers, and removal of the fleet-driven derived refetch), each carrying its own control.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §11 declares `depends-on the-page-paints-from-an-index#s10` in `plan-section-depends-on`, which matches its own closing sentence "Build it after §10, which writes the same files", and no dependency it needs points at a wrong or missing node.
